title: TUI v1: live log navigation with tabs, heartbeat status, and drilldown inspection
description: Build the first production-grade TUI for openclaw-logpulse. Primary unit is individual log events, but the architecture must stay extensible for future grouped views (session, correlated tool calls, tool name, severity, time buckets). Default main layout is split view with a left navigation area and right inspector. Default primary tabs: Events, Correlated Tool Calls, Sessions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Main TUI has Events, Correlated Tool Calls, and Sessions tabs. 2) Heartbeats are removed from the main event list by default and summarized as status instead. 3) Selecting a correlated tool call drills into Events filtered to that call. 4) Selecting a session drills into Correlated Tool Calls filtered to that session. 5) Selecting an event expands inspection so full contents can be examined. 6) UX stays Vim-friendly and slightly polished. 7) Core filters are first-class: session, tool, severity, time window, text search, stale-only. 8) Architecture explicitly leaves room for future grouped views, search/filter panels, and richer session inspection.
close_reason: TUI v1 completed: scoped, implemented, independently reviewed, landed on main at 7cf2646ecaffcc2b10756b3bf85032003667f85f, and installed binary updated/smoke-tested. Future enhancements were explicitly deferred.

title: Implement three-tab primary navigation: Events, Correlated Tool Calls, Sessions
description: Add the main left-side navigation model with three tabs. Events is the default tab and lists individual log events. Correlated Tool Calls lists grouped/correlated tool-call units. Sessions lists active sessions ordered by most recently active first.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Default tab is Events. 2) Correlated Tool Calls tab renders grouped tool-call entries. 3) Sessions tab renders active sessions ordered by latest activity descending. 4) Tab switching has logical Vim-friendly navigation. 5) UI architecture remains compatible with future tabs/modes.

title: Implement drilldown flow between Sessions, Correlated Tool Calls, and Events
description: Implement hierarchical drilldown behavior. Enter on a session should move to the Correlated Tool Calls tab filtered to that session. Enter on a correlated tool-call entry should move to the Events tab filtered to that tool call. Enter on an event should expand inspection for full examination.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Session -> Enter opens Correlated Tool Calls filtered to that session. 2) Correlated Tool Call -> Enter opens Events filtered to that tool call. 3) Event -> Enter expands inspection for full content. 4) Back-navigation returns users to the previous logical context without losing filters unexpectedly.

title: Replace heartbeat event spam with status-bar health signal

acceptance_criteria: 1) Heartbeat events are hidden from the main event list by default. 2) Status bar displays current observed heartbeat health succinctly. 3) Multiple heartbeat events collapse into current-state semantics rather than flooding the buffer. 4) Status behavior has documented defaults and tests.

title: Implement FOLLOW/BROWSE navigation semantics across panes
description:
Current navigation mixes live follow behavior with buffer-style browsing, causing jumpy back-and-forth movement when pressing j repeatedly.

Scope: Events, Tool Calls, and Sessions panes.

Locked semantics:
- Rename mode labels to FOLLOW and BROWSE
- FOLLOW = live tailing behavior
- BROWSE = vim-buffer-style navigation
- Any manual navigation leaves FOLLOW and enters BROWSE
- gg must end at top in BROWSE
- f explicitly re-enters FOLLOW
- G remains normal vim bottom navigation
- scrolloff = 5
- Help/menu must document the follow key

Research note exists on branch `agent/follow-browse-scrollfix` at `notes/follow-browse-scroll-research.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
- repeated j/k navigation no longer jumps back and forth
- incoming rows do not yank the viewport while in BROWSE
- f resumes FOLLOW explicitly
- FOLLOW/BROWSE labels appear in UI/help instead of old naming
- behavior is consistent across Events, Tool Calls, and Sessions
- scrolloff = 5 is enforced in browse mode
